Edge Betweenness Network

Source: R/centrality_measures.R
net_edge_betweenness.Rd

net_edge_betweenness() returns a copy of a network in which each edge's weight is replaced by its betweenness: the number of shortest paths between ordered pairs of distinct nodes that pass through that edge, with a fractional share when several shortest paths tie (Girvan & Newman 2002). It takes a single network or a netobject_group, which is scored one network at a time.

With invert = TRUE (the default) a heavier edge is a shorter step, so the shortest path between two states of a transition network is the most probable route, not the one with the fewest hops. Only positive weights count as edges, and a self-loop never lies on a shortest path, so its betweenness is 0. A directed network gives an asymmetric betweenness matrix; an undirected one a symmetric matrix, each cell holding the betweenness of that edge. The result keeps the source network's directedness (directed when it records none).

An edge with high betweenness carries many of the shortest routes between states; Girvan & Newman (2002) read such edges as the bridges between groups of states. To compare the edge betweenness of two groups, pass two results to permutation() or bayes_compare(), which resample the source networks behind them; both need two results with the same source method and invert, and bayes_compare() needs "relative" source networks.

Usage

net_edge_betweenness(x, invert = TRUE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'netobject'
net_edge_betweenness(x, invert = TRUE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'netobject_group'
net_edge_betweenness(x, invert = TRUE, ...)

# Default S3 method
net_edge_betweenness(x, invert = TRUE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'net_edge_betweenness'
plot(x, style = c("bar", "forest", "delta"), top_n = NULL, labels = TRUE, ...)

Arguments

x

A netobject or netobject_group; any other input raises an error. For the plot() method: a net_edge_betweenness network.

invert

Whether to turn weights into distances by 1 / weight before finding shortest paths, which suits probability and frequency networks. With FALSE, the weight itself is the distance; use it when the weights already are distances. Default TRUE.

...

Not used.

style

For the plot() method: the kind of chart. "bar" (default) draws one horizontal bar per edge; "forest" a stem from zero to a point, with a dashed line at the mean betweenness of the edges shown; "delta" each edge's deviation from that mean as a bar pointing right (above the mean, blue) or left (below, red).

top_n

For the plot() method: the number of highest edges to keep. Default NULL (every edge with non-zero betweenness).

labels

For the plot() method: whether to print each edge's value (its deviation, for "delta") beside it. Default TRUE.

Value

For a netobject: a network of class c("net_edge_betweenness", "netobject", "cograph_network") with method "edge_betweenness", whose weights are the edge betweenness scores. It prints like any network; extract_edges() gives one row per edge, plot() ranks the edges and cograph::splot() draws the network. The source network's data, metadata, parameters, weights and initial probabilities are kept on it, which is what lets permutation() and bayes_compare() test differences in edge betweenness between two such networks. For a netobject_group: a netobject_group of these networks, one per group.

For the plot() method: a ggplot object.

Details

Shortest paths come from all-pairs Floyd-Warshall on the distance matrix (1 / weight, or the weight with invert = FALSE), counting tied paths with a relative tolerance so that floating-point rounding does not break a tie. The values agree with tna::betweenness_network() for transition networks, and on an undirected network each cell equals igraph::edge_betweenness() for that edge; the function is named differently to avoid masking either.

Methods

plot() ranks the edges with non-zero betweenness, highest first, one row per edge (from -> to). It needs no cograph; cograph::splot() draws the same object as a node-link diagram. A network whose edges all have zero betweenness raises an error.

References

Girvan, M. & Newman, M. E. J. (2002). Community structure in social and biological networks. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 99(12), 7821–7826. doi:10.1073/pnas.122653799

Examples

seqs <- data.frame(
  V1 = c("A","B","A","C"), V2 = c("B","C","B","A"),
  V3 = c("C","A","C","B"))
net <- build_network(seqs, method = "relative")
eb  <- net_edge_betweenness(net)
extract_edges(eb)
#>   from to weight
#> 1    C  A      3
#> 2    A  B      3
#> 3    B  C      3
